edition.locus: Gebhardt VII.XVI (the redactor's commission; the tribune)

source_text: Quoniam ergo permisit et permittendo uoluit spiritus sanctus ordinem ipsius muneris conscribi, etsi indigni ad supplementum tantae gloriae describendae, tamen quasi mandatum sanctissimae Perpetuae, immo fideicommissum eius exequimur, unum adicientes documentum de ipsius constantia et animi sublimitate. Cum a tribuno castigatius eo tractantur, quia ex admonitionibus hominum uanissimorum uerebatur ne subtraherentur de carcere incantationibus aliquibus magicis, in faciem ei respondit: Quid utique non permittis nobis refrigerare noxiis nobilissimis, Caesaris scilicet natali depugnaturis? Aut non tua gloria est, si pinguiores illo producamur? Horruit et erubuit tribunus; et ita iussit illos humanius haberi, ut et fratribus eius et ceteris facultas fieret introeundi et refrigerandi cum eis, iam et ipso optione carceris credente.
pass_a_gloss: Since the holy spirit permitted, and by permitting willed, the account of her office to be written down, though we are unworthy to supply the telling of such great glory, still we carry out as it were the order of most holy Perpetua, indeed her trust, adding one evidence of her steadfastness and elevation of soul. Since they were being handled rather harshly by the tribune, because from the warnings of utterly empty men he was afraid they might be removed from prison by some magical spells, she answered him to his face: Why then do you not allow us condemned wretches to take relief, since we are to fight on Caesar's birthday? Or is it not to your credit if we are led out fatter on that day? The tribune trembled and was ashamed; and so he ordered them to be held more kindly, so that both her brothers and the rest got opportunity to come in and take refreshment with them, while now even the prison optio was believing.
pass_b_english: Since the Holy Spirit has permitted the order of her service to be set down, and in permitting it has willed it, we, though unworthy to supply the telling of so great a glory, still carry out the command of most holy Perpetua, indeed her trust committed to us, by adding one more proof of her constancy and loftiness of soul.

For when the tribune was treating them with unusual strictness, because, moved by the warnings of utterly vain men, he feared they might be stolen from prison by certain magical incantations, she answered him to his face: Why do you not allow us poor condemned ones to take relief, since we are to fight on Caesar's birthday? Or will it not be to your own credit if we are led out sleek on that day? The tribune shuddered and was put to shame, and so he ordered them to be kept more humanely, so that both her brothers and the others were given leave to come in and share refreshment with them, while by now even the prison optio himself was believing.

lemmas.gloss: entrusted charge to be carried out
to take relief, to refresh oneself here

choices.english: to take relief / to take refreshment
choices.why: in prison context it means respite with food and visitors, not cooling air, and the infinitive after permittis and facultas fieret governs that prison-visit sense
dative plural substantive agreeing with nobis and depugnaturis, meaning those under sentence of condemnation, with Perpetua using the legal status ironically
ablative of optio, the military subordinate in charge of the prison detail, kept as rank rather than generalized to guard because the clause marks his individual conversion
